english.title: Possess / control article for use in fraud - Fraud Act 2006

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: in the course of or in connection with any fraud

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) had in your possession or under your control an article, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ARTICLE..), for use in the course of or in connection with a fraud
english.legislation: Contrary to section 6 of the Fraud Act 2006.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Mandatory drug test required if 18 or over
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
See H9068 for the " attempt " variation of this Standard Offence Wording document.

(i) Section 8 of the Fraud Act 2006 provides that article includes any program or data held in electronic form.
(ii) Section 12 of the Act makes provision for directors, managers, secretaries or other similar officers or person purporting to act in such a capacity to be liable to prosecution where a body corporate has committed this offence.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Twelve months imprisonment and/or fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

For offences committed before the commencement of section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the penalty is six months imprisonment and/or fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

INDICTMENT: Five years imprisonment and/or fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
NoneOn the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
